content: Probability calibration: Platt scaling (parametric sigmoid, 2 params) beats isotonic regression on small calibration sets (below ~200-1000 examples per Niculescu-Mizil/Caruana; MetricGate: isotonic overfits under ~100 obs per class); isotonic (non-parametric PAVA step function) wins with >=1000 held-out examples. Both are post-hoc layers on held-out data, never training data; evaluate with before/after Brier score, ECE, reliability diagram; if isotonic produces jagged steps the sample is too small. Multi-class markets need one-vs-rest or margin-preserving normalization after per-class calibration.
